messages.author: d6ede225843e2078
messages.subject: Circular plots
parts:
I have a couple of questions about circular plots. I tried looking
some stuff up but there seems to be very little on this topic.

I have activity data for an animal that I have binned for every hour.
I managed to get the plot using coord_polar(), but now I have come
across a few complications,

First of all on my x-axis my "00:00" is not in the center and the
24hours do not seem to distributed evenly (possibly because my time
goes from 0-23???). I would like it that 00:00 is at 0 degrees, 06:00
at 90 degrees, 12:00 at 180 degrees and 18:00 at 270 degrees. I
managed to get this with the clock24.plot in the 'plotrix' but was
hoping to do the same with ggplot2. Is this possible?

Also I want to shade part of my graph. In a normal graph I can just
add a geom_rect, but this does not seem to work when wanting a polar
plot.

Any help would be really appreciated.

messages.author: 27710873736e0505
messages.subject: Re: Circular plots
parts:
hey there,

What you've described is definitely possible, but it would be easier
to help you if you shared some code. I remember doing something with
coord_polor and found the it non-intuitive until I figured out that
the a ray emanating from the origin with angle zero would point strait
up. Things made a lot more sense from there.

geom_rect should work for shading. Have you got you're transformations
strait?

Andrew

messages.author: 73ee81340b5c3c97
messages.subject: RE: Circular plots
parts:
Not perfectly sure this is what you are after -- only read this quickly -- but have you looked at R package CircStats? The stats it covers involve statistics in a circle (sphere, etc.), e.g. clocks, that don't begin at 0 and end at 24 or 360 or whatever -- they are "smooth" and continuous through what ordinary statistics consider a discontinuity.

Not at all an ace on using them, sorry. But a colleague used them to look at reaction rates in a cylindrical vessel with great results. There's a paper that might (or might not) help: google "Circular Dataimages for Directional Data" by Bill Morphet. (Recommend the color version, if you can track it down.)

Ken Johnson
